title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA PRESENTS SANGEET NATAK AKADEMI FELLOWSHIPS AND SANGEET NATAK AKADEMI AWARDS FOR THE YEAR 2024 AND 2025
subtitle: ARTISTS, AS BEARERS OF INDIAN TRADITION, ARE THE GUARDIANS OF OUR COLLECTIVE MEMORY AND THE CREATORS OF OUR VISION FOR THE FUTURE: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
body_text:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu presented Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowships and Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards to the eminent artists for the year 2024 and 2025 in New Delhi today (August 13, 2026).
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that the performing artists honoured today collectively present a cultural map of India—a map woven with stories and songs native to this soil; a map that encompasses the dances and festivals of this diverse land and holds the memories of its languages and dialects, shaped over centuries.
The President said that we possess a multitude of musical traditions, dance styles, and countless forms of folk theatre. Indian culture is deeply rooted in the land. Its diverse culinary traditions, attire, dance forms, and music are all inspired by nature. Artists draw inspiration from chirping birds, babbling waterfalls, trees and foliage, clouds, and rivers to showcase their dance and music. This bond between diversity and unity is one of the greatest strengths of our arts.
The President said that the Guru-Shishya tradition has played a vital role in India's diverse art forms. The Guru serves as the most important book for our arts. In today's rapidly changing times, many of our folk art forms face the threat of extinction. It is essential not only to document such art forms but also to make special efforts to keep them alive. She was happy to note that the Sangeet Natak Akademi is organizing the 'Kala-Diksha' program with this very objective. She urged senior artists to make systematic efforts to groom the next generation.
The President said that nature is considered the most natural training ground for enriching one's life through the values and sensibilities of art. Folk and tribal arts reflect a natural zest for life and a profound communion with nature. In these art forms, the community's memory and collective consciousness find spontaneous expression. That is precisely why folk arts constitute a vital foundation of India's cultural identity.
The President congratulated recipients of Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowships and Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards and said that as bearers of Indian tradition, they are the guardians of our collective memory and the creators of the vision for the future.
The President said that Sangeet Natak Akademi is considered as an important centre of India’s soft power. She expressed confidence that it will continue to enrich the entire world with India's cultural energy in the times to come.

enrichment.summary: President Droupadi Murmu presented the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowships and Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards for 2024 and 2025 to eminent artists in New Delhi on 13 August 2026. In her address, she highlighted India's diverse musical, dance and folk theatre traditions, the importance of the Guru-Shishya parampara, and the need to preserve endangered folk art forms through initiatives like the Akademi's 'Kala-Diksha' programme. She described artists as guardians of collective memory and the Sangeet Natak Akademi as a key centre of India's soft power.
enrichment.context:
The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance and drama, is the oldest of the country's national akademis for the arts, established in 1952 under the Ministry of Culture. It confers the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (Akademi Ratna), the highest honour in performing arts, and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) for outstanding contributions to music, dance, theatre, and traditional/folk/tribal art forms. These awards are significant markers of India's cultural policy framework aimed at recognising, preserving and promoting classical and folk performing arts amid concerns over the erosion of traditional art forms due to modernization and generational shifts away from the Guru-Shishya (teacher-disciple) mode of transmission.

The event underscores the government's emphasis on cultural diplomacy and 'soft power', a concept increasingly used in India's foreign policy and cultural promotion strategy, alongside institutions like ICCR. Programmes such as 'Kala-Diksha' reflect efforts to institutionalise documentation and mentorship for folk and tribal arts, which are often orally transmitted and vulnerable to extinction. This ties into broader UPSC-relevant themes of intangible cultural heritage preservation, similar to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage lists, and India's push to safeguard its diverse artistic traditions as part of national identity and cultural continuity.

prelims_questions.question: The Sangeet Natak Akademi, which confers Fellowships and Awards for performing arts, functions under which Ministry of the Government of India?
prelims_questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance and drama, operates under the Ministry of Culture.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following is the highest honour conferred by the Sangeet Natak Akademi?
prelims_questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship, also known as Akademi Ratna, is the highest honour given by the Akademi, distinct from the annual Akademi Puraskar (Award).
